items.title: Yes, I want to pay for that
items.content:
My last psychiatrist was terrible.

Before every session, you fill out a form talking about how you’re feeling and so on as a way to evaluate whether or not your ADHD meds are working properly. For months, I’d invariably mention something about feeling pretty shitty about the political climate: ICE kidnapping people, trans folks having their very right to exist attacked, and so on.

In our session, she’d ask me, without fail:

But how does that affect personally?

I’m a cishet white male with a strong social net. It doesn’t really affect me at all.

But it affects me because I give a shit about other people, and want to see happy and successful and thriving, and holy shit what an absolutely awful question to ask someone.

I see a similar conversation happen often around social services, like, “why should your taxes pay for…”

  • Other people to go to college?
  • Kids to eat for free at school?
  • Free housing for a homeless person?
  • Candy and junk food for someone on SNAP/food stamps?
  • Someone less healthy than you to have surgery?
  • Rehab for someone struggling with addiction?
  • A vacation or fun experience for someone whose disabled and can’t work?
  • Clothes for someone who can’t afford them?
  • A toy or video game for a kid whose parents don’t work?

The answer is simple: I give a shit about people.

I don’t get why this is weird or confusing or controversial to anyone. I care about people, and I want to see everyone be happy and thrive.

If you want to be a selfish asshole about it, we all do better when we all do better.

  • A better educated population means a better chance of curing chronic illnesses, solving social challenges, and inventing cool new stuff.
  • Kids who aren’t hungry learn better.
  • People who have homes are more likely to work and less likely to use drugs or alcohol.
  • Keeping someone alive means they can work and participate in society.
  • Helping someone beat addiction means can work and participate in society.
  • Keeping people clothed means they can leave the damn house, work, and participate in society.

But like… I don’t give a shit if someone is “productive” or not.

Everyone deserves joy and dignity and compassion, which is why I folks on SNAP or food stamps to be able to buy candy. I want poor people to experience rest and have vacations and for their kids to have toys and fun experiences.

I give a shit about people.

Isn’t it weird how people never ask this question about all of the awful things are taxes actually get used for right now, today? As a US citizen, my taxes are used to…

  • Kidnap minorities and ship them to illegal labor prisons.
  • Clutter space with internet satellites that fuck up astronomy.
  • Poison the water, soil, and air with industrial waste.
  • Rapidly accelerate planetary warming.

I’d much rather some poor kid gets a hot meal or someone who will never work gets to eat a fucking Snickers bar than any of those things.

Because I give a shit about people.

If you’re upset at the idea that your tax money might prevent someone from dying but upset that your taxes are used to literally murder people, you’re the weirdo, not me.

items.title: Life after coding
items.content:
Lately, I’ve been giving a lot of thought to what I would do if I wasn’t a web developer.

I posted about this in a handful of online communities I’m in, and are struggling with these same feelings. If you care about the craft of web work, it’s hard not to feel like the work you love is being ripped away from you.

The trades seem relatively well protected… at least for now. I’m pretty confident I could learn plumbing or electrical work and go into a trade if I wanted to.

But I’ve already changed careers once in my life, and don’t know that I have the energy or financial ability to go through that lengthy process again.

Even for the more lucrative trades like electrical or welding, it would take a handful of years to get back to the level of income I’m making now. And none of them offer the level of work from anywhere flexibility that web work provides.

But so many of my peers across the industry are enthusiastically training their robot replacements or acting like they have no other option but just go along with the inevitable. I’m not sure unionization is actually possible for a lot of people.

AI evangelists spend so much time talking about how AI will free us from drudgery and allow us to spend more time enjoying life.

In reality, it’s stealing all the fun stuff and leaving us with the shit. But even if that weren’t true, they never talk about how you’re supposed to “enjoy life” if you have no money, no home, no food, and no social safety net.

items.title: Wasting Time
items.content:
I saw this on one of the social sites the other day, but I can’t remember which (or who shared it)…

“Wasting time” might be one of the strangest accusations we’ve ever invented. Apparently you can waste 2:00 p.m. by sitting under a tree doing nothing.

The afternoon was going to pass either way. The Earth was going to rotate either way. But because you didn’t convert those hours into money, errands or improvement, we decided the time itself was wasted.

As if simply being alive isn’t enough to justify an afternoon.

items.title: For and against
items.content:
Early in my career, I was web performance and accessibility and building cool things.

But as JavaScript frameworks became increasingly ubiquitous, we saw the things I was start to degrade rapidly. Sites got slower and harder to use.

The web took on a boring sameness.

I spent increasing amounts of my time and energy being JS-heavy tooling like React and abstracting away writing code to NPM modules.

More recently, I’ve been AI. Like the JS libraries of yore, it’s making the web shittier… for the same reasons as JS frameworks, and many new reasons, too.

Friends, I’m so fucking sick of being things.

I want to be things again, but the current state of the web and the tech industry more broadly has made that relatively impossible for me when it comes to web developer topics.

That’s not to say there’s not still good things happening to the web. CSS is having a renaissance!

But the joy is gone .

They knew how. It wasn’t that they didn’t care or didn’t want to. They wanted. They still loved… what it had been.

But as they tried to connect to what had once been so captivating, they felt nothing but yawning absence. A void where they’d once been filled.

That’s essentially how I feel about dev more broadly right now.

I can do the work. I enjoy the rote feeling of wielding an experts tools to practice my craft. It’s meditative, when I get into the coding zone.

But that captivating spark? It’s gone.

I’m writing here a lot less lately because I’ve been finding meaning outside of the web.

I’ve been feeding people through a community farm stand I started out of my home. I’ve been doing outreach to unhoused folks in my area.

I’ve been talking to strangers and reading books and riding my bike and exploring the little nooks and crannies of the new town I call home now.

I should probably write more about those things.
